clue.text: Boy's name very recently admitted

parts.note: something that has just happened happened very recently
someone admitted, say to hospital or a building, is in

explanation.surface: A boy's name has only just been let in, perhaps onto a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy's name' is the definition: the answer is a boy's first name, made from a phrase meaning 'only just arrived'.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin is a common male first name, so it is an example of what the clue asks for.

clue.text: Very merry

definitions.meaning: in British informal speech ... means very, as in ... good

explanation.definitionFit: Jolly is an informal British intensifier and also an adjective for cheerful and festive.

clue.text: In Texas a city like this accepts a financial backer

indicators.note: accepts means the phrase for like this takes in the other pieces

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
a becomes an before the following vowel
an angel is someone who finances a theatrical production

explanation.surface: A Texan city behaves this way, taking on an investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angel' is theatre slang for an investor in a show; the clue's 'a' must become an before a vowel. The city is obscure even to many American solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: San Angelo is a city in west-central Texas, so it is an example of a Texan city.

clue.text: Particular couple

definitions.meaning: a single detail or point in a list
a pair in a romantic relationship

explanation.definitionFit: An item is one detail or entry, and in informal use two people seen together as a pair.

clue.text: Fabulous island finally ejects saint and isn't converted

indicators.note: ejects means the letters for saint are thrown out of the phrase for finally

parts.note: finally means at last, a two-word phrase run together here

indicators.note: converted means the letters of isn't are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A legendary island at last drives out a holy man and is no longer as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejects' takes ST out of AT LAST, leaving ATLA; 'converted' turns ISNT into NTIS. 'finally' looks like a last-letter signal but is the phrase AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the mythical island in Plato's tale, so fabulous here means legendary, from fable.

clue.text: Advance publicity one left behind

definitions.meaning: a preview of a film shown ahead of release
someone who trails behind the rest

explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a film preview, and also anyone who lags at the back of a group.

clue.text: Car was effective for one not needing coach

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
did act means took effect, as a medicine works

explanation.surface: A car worked well for a person who needs no bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' reads as a bus to suit 'Car', but here means a tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: An autodidact is self-taught, so needs no tutor or teacher to learn.

clue.text: Artistic circle in Southampton dockyard

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words Southampton dockyard

explanation.surface: An art group meets in the Southampton docks.
explanation.walkthrough: SouthampTON DOckyard. 'Artistic circle' suggests a group of artists, not a round painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tondo is a round painting or carved relief, literally a circular work of art.

clue.text: Meaningful study of London area mayhem's beginning with foolish behaviour

parts.note: SE is the south-east postal district of London

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of mayhem is taken

parts.note: antics are silly or clownish capers

explanation.surface: A serious study of a London district shows chaos starting with silly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is a London postcode area. 'Meaningful study' is a playful definition: the study of meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the branch of linguistics dealing with meaning, so it is a study of meaning.

clue.text: Child in time keeps cooler

indicators.note: keeps means the word in plus the letter for time holds the cooler inside

parts.note: a fan cools a room

explanation.surface: A child in a timeout stays cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like a comparative or a prison, but is a FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a baby or very young child.

clue.text: Light plane without wings followed by bird

indicators.note: a plane's wings stick out at its sides, so taking them away leaves the word plane without its outer letters

parts.note: a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: A light aircraft that has lost its wings is trailed by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' just joins the two pieces in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of light, so the noun light fits.

clue.text: Triumvir getting third of Rome? Just the opposite

parts.note: Mark Antony was one of the three men of Rome's Second Triumvirate

indicators.note: third of picks out the letter in third place of the word Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler takes a third share of Rome, which is quite the reverse of the expected result.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a third of the empire falling to one triumvir; it is only the third letter of 'Rome'. 'Just' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of contrary meaning, so it is the opposite of another word.

clue.text: Beast providing cover for New Statesman?

indicators.note: providing cover for means the beast wraps itself round the letter for new

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired ox of Tibet

explanation.surface: An animal shields the left-wing magazine New Statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Statesman' reads as the British political weekly; split it and 'Statesman?' is someone from the United States, the question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yank is an American, playfully a person from the States, hence a Statesman.

clue.text: New and old wine definitely settled

indicators.note: New signals that the letters of and old wine are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Fresh and vintage wine have been firmly agreed on for the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of 'New and old'; it is the anagram signal for AND OLD WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nailed down has been fixed firmly and finally, so it is definitely settled.

clue.text: Unsteady but spectacular

definitions.meaning: reeling and lurching on one's feet

explanation.definitionFit: Staggering describes someone tottering, and also something so astonishing it overwhelms.

clue.text: Witness traces top criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of traces top are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: An eyewitness tracks down the chief crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' reads as a noun, the top criminal being traced, but it is the anagram signal working on TRACES TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker, someone who sees an event, so witness is a synonym.

clue.text: Siamese swimmer on train

parts.note: a seal is a swimming marine mammal
to train a gun is to point it

explanation.surface: A Thai person swims beside a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siamese' suggests a person from Siam, but the answer is a Siamese cat colouring; 'on' just stacks SEAL above POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal point is a Siamese cat with dark brown points on a pale coat, a type of the breed.

clue.text: Name a current emirate

parts.note: to dub is to give a name to
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Identify a present-day Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day' but is I, the symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven United Arab Emirates, so it is an example of an emirate.

clue.text: Possibly Vandyke's line as an artist

parts.note: a Vandyke is a pointed beard, so possibly Vandyke's means a beard's, by example
a ley is an alignment of ancient sites, a ley line

explanation.surface: Perhaps the painter Van Dyck's line as an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the painter Van Dyck's style; a Vandyke is a pointed beard, named after his portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrey Beardsley was the English illustrator of the 1890s, known for black-and-white drawings.

clue.text: On and on in midst of social group

indicators.note: in means the second on is placed inside those central letters
midst of picks the letters in the middle of the phrase social group, straddling the gap between the words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A party goes on and on, deep in the heart of a social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The central letters straddle the word gap in the two-word phrase. Chambers barely supports the definition; Collins allows it in phrases like 'move along'.
explanation.definitionFit: Along is used as an adverb meaning forward or onward, as in move along, so on is a synonym.

clue.text: Linnaeus may have determined this part of an artist's training

definitions.meaning: the Swedish naturalist sorted living things into ranks of classification, so he decided which group of living things each belonged to
a session drawing from a nude model, a standard part of art school

explanation.definitionFit: A life class is drawing from a live model, and read literally it is a taxonomic class of living things.

clue.text: Send up essayist for bloomer

parts.note: to lob is to send a ball high up in the air
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: Mock a writer of essays for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake but means a flowering plant; 'Send up' reads as mock.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flowering plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Composer upfront about origin of cantata

indicators.note: about means the word for upfront goes around the letter

parts.note: frank means candid, open, upfront

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of cantata

explanation.surface: A composer is candid about where his cantata came from.
explanation.walkthrough: César Franck was a Belgian-born French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: César Franck was a nineteenth-century composer of organ and orchestral music.

clue.text: Wild boar and viper left like poor cat i' the adage?

definitions.text: like poor cat i' the adage?

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of boar and viper run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A savage pig and a snake are left like the cat in the old saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Lady Macbeth's 'like the poor cat i' the adage', the cat that wanted fish but would not wet its feet; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat of the adage is a proverbial cat, one that features in a well-known saying.

clue.text: Without employment, there's nothing left for bird

indicators.note: without means outside, so the letters for nothing and left go around the word for employment

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
use means employment, as in put to use

explanation.surface: Out of work, nothing remains for the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but means outside here, an old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An ousel is an old name for the blackbird, and also the ring ousel, a type of thrush.

clue.text: In vain I would play, ignoring the odds

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means only the even-placed letters of play are kept, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Pointlessly I would play, careless of the betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' sounds like reckless gambling; it keeps the 2nd and 4th letters of PLAY, L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something idly means doing it to no purpose, so it is done in vain.

clue.text: Story involving last bit of Chile pine

indicators.note: involving means the tale wraps round the letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tale

indicators.note: last bit of means the final letter of Chile

explanation.surface: A tale about the last stand of a Chilean pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' reads as a tree, especially beside Chile and its monkey-puzzle pines, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long or ache for something, a synonym of the verb pine.

clue.text: Box not entirely free

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for free loses its final letter

parts.note: spare means free or unoccupied, as in spare time

explanation.surface: A box that is not completely free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is a verb, to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box for practice, so box is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Implant not out yet

parts.note: a cricket batsman not out is still in
yet means still, as in still to come

explanation.surface: Plant something firmly when the batter is not yet dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is 'not out' is IN, still batting.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to implant it gradually in someone's mind, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Star with carbon copy quite taken aback

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape is to copy or mimic

indicators.note: taken aback means the word for quite is turned round

parts.note: quite means all, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A celebrity is startled to see a carbon copy of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reads as 'surprised' but reverses ALL to LLA; 'carbon copy' is two pieces, C and APE.
explanation.definitionFit: Capella is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga, so it is an example of a star.

clue.text: Message rejecting Mrs Simpson from leaders left Edward throneless

indicators.note: rejecting means the whole run of letters is thrown back, read right to left

parts.note: Marge is the wife of Homer in the cartoon The Simpsons

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of left, Edward and throneless

explanation.surface: A cable spurning Wallis Simpson told how Edward VIII gave up the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Wallis Simpson and the 1936 abdication; the Mrs Simpson here is the cartoon Marge. MARGE plus LET is reversed whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by wire and delivered on paper.

clue.text: Draw fish in study

indicators.note: in means the fish goes inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Sketch a fish in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' reads as a room but is CON, to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Crayon is used as a verb meaning to draw or colour with a wax stick, so draw is a synonym.
